messages:
customer-jordan: hey, hitting an embedding issue since last night. When we send batch input (size 2+) to /v1/embeddings with model=redwood-embed-768 we’re seeing vectors of length 1536. Single inputs return 768 as expected. p95 latency also jumped ~3x. API key/auth okay, billing fine. request_id=req_e9f4a2c. Can someone triage?

maya (support): thanks — can you paste a minimal curl + response you saw? also which region?

customer-jordan: sure — EU region. repro:
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-768","input":["hello","world"]}'
```
response:
```json
{"data":[{"embedding":[0.0123, ... /* total 1536 floats */ ...],"object":"embedding"}],"model":"redwood-embed-768","usage":{}}
```
single-input (input: "hello") returns an embedding length 768.

maya (support): noted. @nate can you pick this up? attaching req id. :eyes:

nate (eng-ml): looking now. initial thought: sounds like a model-variant mismatch on batching path (one variant returns 1536 dim). Do you have the full response headers + x-request-trace id? also the exact timestamp helps.

customer-jordan: headers included: `x-request-id: req_e9f4a2c` and `x-request-trace: tr_7b9c` timestamp 2026-03-16T22:14:05Z. attaching raw body (trimmed).

nate (eng-ml): pulled trace tr_7b9c from tracing service. copying relevant spans (summarized):
```
span: auth_verify          6ms
span: routing_decision    18ms  -> routed to embeddings.route.eu-west-1
span: batching_queue      95ms  (batch_size=2)
span: model_variant_select 4ms  -> selected variant: redwood-embed-1536-quant
span: model_infer         322ms
span: postproc_encode     8ms
http_response_total      463ms
```
looks like when batched your requests hit a 1536-dim variant. single requests went to the 768 variant (fast path). we recently rolled a variant swap for traffic shaping.

rachel (eng-platform): deploy-bot shows a rollout at 2026-03-16T21:50:12Z: `feature/model-variant-weighting` -> increased weight of redwood-embed-1536-quant for embeddings.route.eu-west-1 canary.
\
deploy-bot: deploy feature/model-variant-weighting @rachel — completed in 45s — rollout 30% -> 60%

nate (eng-ml): that matches. hypothesis: batching logic doesn't normalize dims when splitting between variants. for batch>1, the router sometimes composes a mixed-variant batch which forces the higher-dim representation. need to confirm if postproc is concatenating instead of rejecting.

maya (support): customer — we can either rollback the rollout or force your requests to the 768-only route while we fix. which do you prefer?

customer-jordan: rollback preferred for now, we can't tolerate the dim mismatch. Also the p95 latency spike is blocking our SLAs.

rachel (eng-platform): rolling back canary to previous weights now. ETA ~5m. I’ll also pin their account to model redwood-embed-768-only as a short-term fix.

rachel (eng-platform): rollback complete at 2026-03-16T22:25:10Z. can you re-test?

customer-jordan: re-tested — batch returns 768 vectors now. latency back to normal. thank you.

nate (eng-ml): next steps: 1) patch router batching logic to ensure variant homogeneity per-batch (reject or reroute mismatched variant candidates). 2) add a validation step that fails fast with clear error when model dims don't match expected. 3) add unit/e2e test for batching + variant weighting.

maya (support): ops: can you add a dashboard tile for quick detection? recommend: embeddings.route.dim_counts, embeddings.batch_size.dist, embeddings.p95_by_model_variant. link: https://console.redwood.ai/d/embeddings/overview?panelId=dim-tracker

rachel (eng-platform): added alert: embeddings.dim.mismatch.rate > 0.5% for 5m -> page on-call. also created a short-lived runbook for rollback steps.

nate (eng-ml): logging note: include model_variant id in trace and response headers `x-variant-id` so we can debug faster next time.

maya (support): tagging this resolved for customer; leaving open for eng action items. Jordan — we’ll follow up when patch lands. :thumbsup:

customer-jordan: super helpful, thanks everyone!
